Getting started
The Multiversal Vehicle Controller API exposes every vehicle system and component so you can script custom behaviours, extend existing classes, or integrate MVC with your own architecture. Download the toolkit from [https://mvc.gg/download](mvc.gg) and open the `Packages/dev.bxbstudio.mvc` folder to begin browsing the API.
This API Manual assumes you are comfortable with C# and Unity's component workflow. Each section lists inheritance graphs, method summaries and short code snippets you can paste into your own scripts.
MVC
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-ijobdatarefreshable](IJobDataRefreshable) Represents a runtime owner that can defer job-data refreshes to a safe scheduling boundary.
[#mvc-jobdatarefreshflags](JobDataRefreshFlags) Selects the managed configuration snapshots that should be copied into job-safe data.
[#mvc-jobdatarefreshqueue](JobDataRefreshQueue) Allocation-free accumulator used by job-data owners at their scheduling boundary.
[#mvc-toolkitbehaviour](ToolkitBehaviour) Base MonoBehaviour class that provides core functionality and static access to MVC toolkit components. This class serves as the foundation for all MVC toolkit behaviors and provides centralized access to essential services like settings, vehicle management, UI control, and audio.
[#mvc-toolkitbehaviourextension`1](ToolkitBehaviourExtension`1) Generic extension class that provides a base reference to a specific ToolkitBehaviour type. This class is useful for components that need to access their parent or sibling ToolkitBehaviour components without direct inheritance.
[#mvc-toolkitcomponent](ToolkitComponent) Serializable component class that provides static access to MVC toolkit services. This class can be used as a field in other components to access toolkit functionality without requiring MonoBehaviour inheritance.
[#mvc-toolkitscriptableobject](ToolkitScriptableObject) Base ScriptableObject class that provides static access to MVC toolkit services. This class can be inherited by other ScriptableObjects to access toolkit functionality without requiring MonoBehaviour inheritance.
[#mvc-toolkitsettings](ToolkitSettings) Main settings asset for the MVC toolkit. Stores all global configuration, presets, and references for the toolkit. This class is a ScriptableObject and is intended to be used as a singleton asset.
[#mvc-vehicleaudiosource](VehicleAudioSource) VehicleAudioSource is a utility component for managing an AudioSource in the context of vehicle systems. It provides convenient methods to play, pause, stop, and control the enabled state of the AudioSource, including support for playing a clip once (optionally with a delay) and then disabling the AudioSource. This is useful for managing one-shot or event-driven audio in vehicle systems, such as engine sounds, collision effects, or other transient audio cues.
[#mvc-vehiclemanager](VehicleManager) Central manager class for the Multiversal Vehicle Controller system. Handles vehicle registration, player management, ground mapping, and global system coordination. This class serves as a singleton that manages all active vehicles, AI vehicles, and player interactions.
AI
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-ai-vehicleailayer](VehicleAILayer) Represents an AI layer for vehicles in the MVC system. AI layers allow grouping and organizing vehicle AI behaviors with unique names.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower](VehicleAIPathFollower) VehicleAIPathFollower is an AI behaviour for vehicles that enables them to follow a predefined path (VehicleAIPath). It supports obstacle detection, lead vehicle following, zone-based behaviour (brake, handbrake, NOS), and dynamic steering/throttle input calculation. The class manages path progress, obstacle avoidance, corner anticipation, and recovery from stuck situations.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaitargetfollower](VehicleAITargetFollower) VehicleAITargetFollower is an AI behaviour for vehicles that enables them to follow a moving or static target using Unity's NavMeshAgent. This class manages the creation and configuration of a NavMeshAgent for the vehicle, allowing it to navigate the environment, avoid obstacles, and follow a target dynamically. It is intended for use in scenarios where the vehicle must pursue a target rather than follow a predefined path.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaizone](VehicleAIZone) VehicleAIZone defines a special zone along a VehicleAIPath that modifies AI vehicle behavior. Zones can be of type Brake, Handbrake, or NOS, and each type applies specific input modifications (such as braking intensity, speed targets, slip, or NOS minimums) to vehicles that enter the zone. This class exposes properties for configuring the effect of the zone and provides editor visualization. Check the class for more information.

VehicleAIPath
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-buildgroundraycastcommandsjob](BuildGroundRaycastCommandsJob) Burst-compiled job for building batched ground raycasts for every spaced path point. This keeps the expensive query setup in native memory before the physics batch is scheduled.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-curvetype](CurveType) Defines the mathematical curve type used for path generation and interpolation.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-curvesdistancetablesjob](CurvesDistanceTablesJob) Burst-compiled job for calculating distance tables for Bezier curves. This job computes the length of each curve and accumulates the total path length.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-generatepointsjob](GeneratePointsJob) Burst-compiled job for generating evenly spaced points along the path. This job creates a series of points at regular intervals along each curve.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-groundalignmentcandidate](GroundAlignmentCandidate) Represents one eligible ground candidate for a spaced path point. Stores both the resolved surface data and the metrics used during continuity scoring.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-groundalignmentfirstdeckpolicy](GroundAlignmentFirstDeckPolicy) Defines how the first ambiguous stacked-road ground candidate is selected.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-spacedpathpoint](SpacedPathPoint) Represents a point along a spaced path with reference to its parent curve. This structure maintains the relationship between path points and their source curves.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipath-visualizermeshanchor](VisualizerMeshAnchor) Internal structure for storing visualizer mesh anchor data. Contains all necessary information for rendering the path visualizer.
Fields
Name Description
DEFAULT_VEHICLE_FRICTION_FOR_VELOCITY_EVALUATION Default vehicle friction value used for velocity evaluation calculations. This value represents a typical friction coefficient for road vehicles.
DEFAULT_ZONE_BRAKE_SPEED_TARGET Brake speed target in km/h given to a brake zone placed where the path does not corner, and therefore has no cornering limit of its own to derive one from.
GROUND_ALIGNMENT_MAX_HITS Maximum number of ground hits inspected per path point during multi-floor alignment. This caps the search cost while still allowing stacked-road candidates to compete.
GROUND_ALIGNMENT_MIN_COMMANDS_PER_JOB Minimum number of commands grouped into each batch job when scheduling the ground queries.
GROUND_ALIGNMENT_MIN_SEGMENT Shortest segment between two aligned points that may be used to measure curvature. Anything shorter is dominated by the noise of the ground query rather than by the road's shape.
PATH_VISUALIZER_HEAT_RANGE How far over a point's target velocity, in m/s, the visualizer takes to reach full heat.
VISUALIZER_NAME The name used for the path visualizer GameObject in the scene.
bezier Legacy Bezier path data for backward compatibility.
bezierCurves Array of Bezier curves defining the path.
cardinalScale Scale factor for Cardinal spline interpolation.
curveType The mathematical curve type used for path generation and interpolation.
curvesLength Array storing the length of each individual curve.
drawWidth Width of the path for drawing and visualization.
firstPoint First point of the path when no curves exist.
firstPointHasValue Whether the firstPoint has a valid value.
followerCameras Array of cameras that follow the path for visualization.
generatedPathLengthSamples Number of samples used when generating the path length.
groundAlignmentContinuityBias Weight used to prefer candidates that remain on the same deck as neighbouring points. Higher values make stacked-road continuity more important than matching the raw raycast distance.
groundAlignmentFirstDeckPolicy Selects how the first ambiguous stacked-road point seeds deck continuity.
groundAlignmentMaxContinuityDelta Maximum vertical delta allowed before a candidate is treated as a deck switch. Candidates beyond this threshold are heavily penalized to keep the path on the current floor.
groundAlignmentSearchHeight Vertical search range below the point when resolving stacked or overlapping ground surfaces. Larger values allow the path to inspect more decks before choosing a ground candidate.
groundDetectionRayHeight Height above the path for ground detection raycasts. Must be greater than math.EPSILON.
groundLayerMask Layer mask defining which layers are considered ground for path alignment.
hermiteCurves Array of Hermite curves defining the path.
isShowingVisualizer Whether the visualizer is currently being displayed.
loopedPath Whether the path forms a closed loop.
selectedGizmoMesh Reused mesh for selected path gizmo rendering in the Scene view.
showHideCoroutine Coroutine for handling show/hide animations of the visualizer.
showHideInProgress Whether a show/hide operation is currently in progress.
showVisualizerAtStart Whether to automatically show the visualizer when the path is created.
snapZones Whether to enable snapping to predefined zones along the path.
spacedPoints Array of evenly spaced points along the path.
spacedPointsSpacing Distance between consecutive spaced points.
startOffset Offset distance from the start of the path where vehicles begin.
totalLength Total length of the entire path in world units.
useCardinal Whether Cardinal spline interpolation is enabled.
visualizer GameObject reference for the path visualizer in the scene.
visualizerAnchorDistances Array of distances from the start of the path to each visualizer anchor.
visualizerAnchors Array of mesh anchor data for the visualizer.
visualizerClosestPointIndex Last resolved closest spaced-point index, used by the visualizer's incremental local search. -1 marks the cache as invalid (forces a full scan on the next resolve).
visualizerColors Persistent vertex colour buffer, reused every frame to avoid the per-frame allocation that get/set would otherwise incur.
visualizerFilter Mesh filter component for the visualizer mesh.
visualizerMesh Cached instance mesh of the visualizer, used to push per-frame vertex colours without re-fetching it.
visualizerRenderer Mesh renderer component for the visualizer mesh.
visualizerShowHidePointDuration Duration for showing/hiding individual visualizer points. Must be greater than 0.
visualizerSpeedMultiplier Multiplier for the visualizer animation speed. Range: 0.0 to 2.0.
Methods
Name Description
AddAIZone(UnityEngine.Vector3, MVC.AI.VehicleAIZone.AIZoneType) Adds a new AI zone of the specified type at the given world position. If the zone is a Brake zone, its target speed is set based on the closest path point. Optionally snaps the zone to the nearest path point if snapping is enabled.
AddAudioZone(UnityEngine.Vector3, MVC.Base.VehicleAudioZone.AudioZoneType) Not implemented: Adding audio zones is not supported for AI paths. AI paths are designed for vehicle navigation and do not support audio zone functionality.
AddDamageZone(UnityEngine.Vector3, MVC.Base.VehicleDamageZone.DamageZoneType) Not implemented: Adding damage zones is not supported for AI paths. AI paths are designed for vehicle navigation and do not support damage zone functionality.
AddNextCurve(Unity.Mathematics.float3) Adds a new curve to the end of the path at the specified position. This method extends the path by adding a new curve segment.
AddNextCurve(Unity.Mathematics.float3, MVC.Utilities.BezierCurve@, MVC.Utilities.HermiteCurve@) Adds a new curve to the end of the path and returns the created curve objects. This overload provides access to the created curve objects for further manipulation.
AddWeatherZone(UnityEngine.Vector3, MVC.Base.VehicleWeatherZone.WeatherZoneType) Not implemented: Adding weather zones is not supported for AI paths. AI paths are designed for vehicle navigation and do not support weather zone functionality.
AlignSpacedPointsToGround Aligns the generated path points to the ground using raycasts.
ApplyAlignedCurvature(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@, Unity.Mathematics.float3) Writes a measured curvature vector into a point, splitting it against that point's aligned frame.
ApplyGroundAlignmentCandidate(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate) Applies the resolved candidate to a spaced path point. The path tangent is preserved while the up/right basis is rebuilt from the chosen surface.
ApplyPreviousDeckFallback(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@, MVC.Utilities.CurvePoint) Reuses the previous resolved deck when the current point could not be resolved confidently. This intentionally avoids snapping to a lower bridge/underpass hit when continuity data is weak.
Awake Unity Awake callback. Ensures the path is initialized only once. Calls to set up the path system.
CalculateCurvesLength Calculates the length of all curves in the path.
CalculateCurvesLength(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.Utilities.BezierCurve}@, Unity.Collections.NativeArray{System.Single}@) Calculates the length of all curves in the path using the job system.
ClosestCurveIndex(Unity.Mathematics.float3) Finds the index of the curve closest to the given position.
ClosestCurveIndex(Unity.Mathematics.float3, System.Single) Finds the index of the curve closest to the given position within a maximum distance.
ClosestCurveIndexFast(Unity.Mathematics.float3) Quickly finds the index of the curve closest to the given position by only checking curve endpoints. Less accurate but faster than ClosestCurveIndex.
ClosestSpacedPointIndex(Unity.Mathematics.float3) Finds the index of the spaced point closest to the given position. This method searches through all spaced points to find the closest one.
ClosestSpacedPointIndex(Unity.Mathematics.float3, System.Int32, System.Int32) Finds the index of the spaced point closest to the given position within a range of indices. This method performs a linear search through a specified range of points for optimal performance.
ClosestSpacedPointIndex(Unity.Mathematics.float3, System.Single) Finds the index of the spaced point closest to the given position within a maximum distance.
CopyCurvature(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint) Copies every curvature field from one point to another, leaving the rest of the target untouched.
CreatePathVisualizer Creates a visual representation of the AI path in the scene.
DrawPathVisualizer Generates and updates the mesh for the path visualizer.
EvaluateSpacedPointSteerAngle(System.Int32, System.Single) Calculates the steering angle for a vehicle at the specified spaced point.
GenerateSpacedPoints Generates evenly spaced points along the path curves for AI navigation. This method creates a series of points at regular intervals along each curve for smooth AI movement.
GetArgumentOutOfRangeException(System.String, System.Object, System.Int32) Creates an ArgumentOutOfRangeException with a formatted message.
GetCurveLength(System.Int32) Gets the length of a specific curve in the path. This method provides access to pre-calculated curve lengths for performance.
GetCurveSpacedPoints(System.Int32, System.Boolean) Gets an array of spaced points for a specific curve.
GetCurveSpacedPoints(System.Int32, Unity.Collections.NativeList{MVC.Utilities.SpacedCurvePoint}, System.Boolean) Populates a NativeList with spaced points for a specific curve.
GetGroundAlignmentCandidate(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate}, System.Int32, System.Int32) Reads one candidate from the flat candidate buffer.
GetGroundAlignmentCandidateBaseIndex(System.Int32) Returns the start index of a point's candidate segment within the flat candidate buffer.
GetNextCurveIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@) Gets the index of the next curve after the specified curve index. This method handles both linear and looped paths, wrapping around for looped paths.
GetNextCurveIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@, MVC.Utilities.BezierCurve@) Gets the index and Bezier curve of the next curve after the specified curve index. This overload provides both the index and the actual Bezier curve object.
GetNextCurveIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@, MVC.Utilities.HermiteCurve@) Gets the index and Hermite curve of the next curve after the specified curve index. This overload provides both the index and the actual Hermite curve object.
GetNextSpacedPointIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@) Gets the index of the next spaced point after the specified point index.
GetNextSpacedPointIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@) Gets the index and data of the next spaced point after the specified point index. This overload provides both the index and the actual SpacedPathPoint data.
GetPreviousCurveIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@) Gets the index of the previous curve before the specified curve index. This method handles both linear and looped paths, wrapping around for looped paths.
GetPreviousCurveIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@, MVC.Utilities.BezierCurve@) Gets the index and bezier curve of the previous curve before the specified curve index.
GetPreviousCurveIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@, MVC.Utilities.HermiteCurve@) Gets the index and hermite curve of the previous curve before the specified curve index.
GetPreviousSpacedPointIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@) Gets the index of the previous spaced point before the specified point index.
GetPreviousSpacedPointIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32@, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@) Gets the index and data of the previous spaced point before the specified point index.
GetSpacedPoint(System.Int32) Gets a spaced path point at the specified index, handling looped paths.
HidePathVisualizer Hides the path visualizer with a smooth animation. This method makes the path invisible to reduce visual clutter during gameplay.
Initialize Resets all runtime fields and destroys any existing visualizer objects. Used internally before reinitializing the path.
InverseCurvePosition(System.Int32, Unity.Mathematics.float3) Finds the parametric t-value on a curve closest to the given position.
LateUpdate Updates the path visualization each frame after other updates are complete.
LoopIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32) Returns a valid index within the range [0, pointsCount), wrapping around if necessary. Useful for looping path indices and ensuring they stay within bounds.
MergeCurves(System.Int32, System.Int32) Merges two curves into a single curve. This method combines two adjacent curves into one, maintaining the overall path shape.
NewPath Creates a new path with a single default curve starting at the current position. This method initializes a basic path structure that can be expanded upon.
OffsetCurves(Unity.Mathematics.float3) Offsets all curves in the path by the specified vector.
OnDrawGizmosSelected Draws debug visualization of the path in the Scene view when the object is selected. This method provides comprehensive visual feedback for path editing and debugging.
PackGroundAlignmentCandidates(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{UnityEngine.RaycastHit}, Unity.Collections.NativeArray{Unity.Mathematics.float3}, Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate}, Unity.Collections.NativeArray{System.Int32}, System.Int32) Copies the batched raycast results into a flat candidate buffer indexed by point and hit order. This keeps the expensive physics queries in native memory while preserving the existing continuity resolver.
RefreshAlignedCurvatures(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint[]) Recomputes the curvature of every spaced point from the positions of its aligned neighbours. Ground alignment moves the points onto the terrain, so the curvature baked in from the analytic spline stops describing the path the vehicle actually drives. Left alone it disagrees with the aligned positions exactly where the terrain is least flat, which is where target speeds matter.
RefreshCardinal Refreshes the cardinal spline calculations and syncs with Bezier curves.
RefreshPathVisualizer Updates the path visualizer's appearance based on player position and vehicle stats.
RemoveCurve(System.Boolean) Removes a curve from either the start or end of the path.
RemoveFirstCurve Removes the first curve in the path. This method removes the curve at index 0 and shifts all remaining curves down.
RemoveLastCurve Removes the last curve in the path. This method removes the curve at the highest index and reduces the array size.
Reset Resets the path to its default state by clearing all curves and points. This method provides a public interface to reset the path completely.
ResetPath Resets the path to an empty state, clearing all curves and points. This method completely clears the path data and resets to default values.
ResolveAlignedKappaVector(Unity.Mathematics.float3, Unity.Mathematics.float3, Unity.Mathematics.float3) Measures the curvature vector of the middle of three consecutive positions.
ResolvePathVisualizerHeat(System.Single, System.Single) Resolves how hot a path point should read, from 0 for comfortably within the limit to 1 for well over it.
ResolveVisualizerClosestPointIndex(Unity.Mathematics.float3) Resolves the spaced point closest to for the visualizer, using an incremental local search around the previously resolved index instead of a full O(N) scan.
ResolveZoneBrakeSpeedTarget(MVC.Utilities.CurvePoint) Resolves the speed a brake zone should slow a vehicle down to at a given path point.
Restart Restarts and reinitializes the AI path, regenerating all path data and visualizers. This method is typically called during Awake or when the path needs to be rebuilt.
SelectGroundAlignmentReferenceHeight(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate}, System.Int32, System.Int32, System.Single) Chooses the candidate height closest to a preferred deck height. Used only for continuity hints, not for the final point orientation.
SelectHighestGroundAlignmentCandidate(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate}, System.Int32, System.Int32) Chooses the highest valid candidate for a point. Used only when a caller explicitly wants generated paths to seed continuity from the upper deck.
SetCurvesWidth(System.Single) Sets the width of all curves in the path to the specified value.
ShowHidePathVisualizer(System.Boolean) Internal method to handle showing or hiding the path visualizer with animation.
ShowHidePathVisualizerCoroutine(System.Boolean, System.Single) Coroutine that handles the fade animation when showing/hiding the path visualizer.
ShowPathVisualizer Shows the path visualizer with a smooth animation. This method makes the path visible to help with debugging and path editing.
SplitCurve(System.Int32, Unity.Mathematics.float3) Splits an existing curve into two curves at the specified position. This method uses de Casteljau's algorithm to maintain curve continuity and quality.
SyncBezierHermiteCurves Synchronizes Bezier and Hermite curve representations using the current curve type.
SyncBezierHermiteCurves(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.CurveType) Synchronizes Bezier and Hermite curve representations based on the specified source curve type.
TryGetGroundAlignmentLookAheadHeight(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate}, Unity.Collections.NativeArray{System.Int32}, System.Int32, System.Single, System.Single@) Searches forward for the next point that has at least one valid ground candidate. This provides a stable seed height when the current point is the first ambiguous point in the path.
TryGetSpacedPoint(System.Int32, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint@) Attempts to get a spaced path point at the specified index.
TryLoadLegacyBezierPath Attempts to load and convert legacy Bezier path data.
TryResolveCurvatureNeighbours(System.Int32, System.Int32, System.Int32@, System.Int32@) Resolves the neighbours used to measure a point's curvature.
TryResolveGroundAlignmentCandidate(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint[], Unity.Collections.NativeArray{MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate}, Unity.Collections.NativeArray{System.Int32}, System.Int32, System.Boolean, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.GroundAlignmentCandidate@) Resolves the best ground candidate for a point by preserving deck continuity across neighbours. The previous resolved point is the primary anchor; if none exists, the method seeds continuity from a look-ahead point.

RefreshAlignedCurvatures(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPath.SpacedPathPoint[])
Recomputes the curvature of every spaced point from the positions of its aligned neighbours. Ground alignment moves the points onto the terrain, so the curvature baked in from the analytic spline stops describing the path the vehicle actually drives. Left alone it disagrees with the aligned positions exactly where the terrain is least flat, which is where target speeds matter.

VehicleAIPathFollower
VehicleAIPathFollower is an AI behaviour for vehicles that enables them to follow a predefined path (VehicleAIPath). It supports obstacle detection, lead vehicle following, zone-based behaviour (brake, handbrake, NOS), and dynamic steering/throttle input calculation. The class manages path progress, obstacle avoidance, corner anticipation, and recovery from stuck situations.
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-followdirection](FollowDirection) Determines the direction in which the AI follows the path.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-obstacledetectionmethod](ObstacleDetectionMethod) Determines the method used for obstacle detection.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-pedalinputtargets](PedalInputTargets) The resolved pedal demands for a single update, before interpolation.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-recoverystate](RecoveryState) The stages of the stuck detection and reverse recovery manoeuvre.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-sensorsample](SensorSample) The resolved reading of a single obstacle sensor for the current update.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-startpoint](StartPoint) Determines how the AI selects its starting point on the path.
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaipathfollower-trafficpolicy](TrafficPolicy) Determines how the AI behaves towards other vehicles sharing the path.
Fields
Name Description
AI_APPROACH_BRAKE_MARGIN The fraction of the brake capacity the corner approach plans with. Planning with all of it puts the end of the braking zone inside the corner, where braking and turning share one grip budget; the margin moves the braking earlier so it is done before the turn-in. It also buys time for the smoothed grip readings behind the stability ceilings, which lag the car by a few tenths of a second, to catch up before the corner load peaks.
AI_BACKWARD_SLIDE_BRAKE_SPEED The backwards speed (in km/h) past which a vehicle in a forward gear brakes to arrest the slide instead of applying throttle.
AI_FALLBACK_BRAKING_TIME How many seconds of braking to assume when the vehicle cannot report a usable braking distance, which happens while it is airborne and has no grip to brake against.
AI_MIN_CORNER_VELOCITY The slowest a corner may ever ask the vehicle to go, in m/s. A corner limit of zero means the corner cannot be taken at any speed, which is never something the vehicle can act on: at zero it applies no throttle, so it never moves, so it stays at zero. Crawling is the recoverable answer.
AI_MIN_EXTREMUM_SLIP The smallest extremum slip the grip utilization will divide by.
AI_RACING_GAP_SCALE Scales the follow gap down when the traffic policy is set to Racing.
AI_RECOVERY_RESET_ADVANCE How much further along the path (in meters) each successive path reset at the same trap lands.
AI_RECOVERY_RESET_MAX_STEPS The most reset steps the advance may escalate to, so the landing point never runs away around the whole path.
AI_REJOIN_DISTANCE_SCALE How many times the path advance distance the vehicle may stray from its current path point before the rejoin speed limit kicks in.
AI_REJOIN_MIN_DISTANCE The distance from the current path point under which the rejoin speed limit never engages, in meters, so a small advance distance cannot make it flicker during normal driving.
AI_REJOIN_TARGET_SPEED The speed the vehicle limits itself to while it is far away from the path, in km/h.
AI_REVERSE_SHIFT_TIMEOUT How long to wait for a requested gear shift to actually engage before giving up on it.
AI_SENSOR_ANGLE_REFERENCE_VELOCITY The speed (in m/s) at which the diagonal sensors reach their narrowest spread.
OBSTACLE_RAYCAST_SENSORS_COUNT The number of raycast sensors used for obstacle detection (front, front-left, front-right, left, right).
brakeZones List of active brake zones the vehicle is currently inside.
currentPathPoint The current spaced path point being targeted.
currentPathPointPosition The world position of the current path point.
diagonalSensorsAngle The diagonal sensors spread for the current update, in degrees.
diagonalSensorsDynamicSteerIntensity Steering intensity for diagonal sensors (dynamic obstacles). Ignored when the traffic policy is set to Traffic.
diagonalSensorsMaxAngle The spread of the diagonal sensors at a standstill, in degrees.
diagonalSensorsMinAngle The spread of the diagonal sensors at speed, in degrees.
diagonalSensorsSteerIntensity Steering intensity for diagonal sensors (static obstacles).
followDirection The direction in which to follow the path.
followMinimumGap The gap to keep behind a stationary lead vehicle, in meters. Halved when the traffic policy is set to Racing.
followTimeGap The time gap to keep behind a lead vehicle, in seconds. Halved when the traffic policy is set to Racing.
followVelocityLimit The velocity cap imposed by the lead vehicle, in m/s.
frameBrakeAcceleration The deceleration the brakes can deliver this update, in m/s^2.
frameBrakingDistance The distance needed to stop from the current speed this update, in meters. Always finite.
frameCorneringFriction The sideways wheels friction available for cornering this update.
frameDeltaTime The delta time for the current update.
frameFrontLateralGripUse How much of the front axle's lateral grip is being used this update, where 1 is its limit.
frameIsReversing Whether the vehicle is currently travelling backwards on purpose.
framePathFriction The wheels friction available for path and braking calculations this update.
frameRearLateralGripUse How much of the rear axle's lateral grip is being used this update, where 1 is its limit.
frameSignedSpeed The signed forward speed for the current update, in km/h. Negative while moving backwards.
frameStabilityBrakeCeiling The most brake the vehicle can take this update without losing grip, from 0 to 1.
frameStabilityFuelCeiling The most throttle the vehicle can take without spinning its driven wheels this update.
frameStats The vehicle stats snapshot for the current update.
frameTargetVelocity The velocity the AI is currently trying to reach, in m/s.
frameTravelVelocity The speed along the current travel direction for the current update, in m/s. Always positive when moving as intended.
gravity The magnitude of gravity (used for physics calculations).
handbrakeZones List of active handbrake zones the vehicle is currently inside.
hasLeadVehicle Whether a lead vehicle has been detected ahead on the path.
isQueuedBehindLead Whether the AI is deliberately queuing behind a moving lead rather than being stuck.
lastFollowDirection The last follow direction used (for change detection).
lastFuelPedalTarget The fuel demand resolved on the previous update, used by the stuck test.
lastPath The last path assigned to this AI (for change detection).
leadStationaryTimer How long the lead vehicle has been stationary, in seconds.
leadVehicleDistance The gap to the lead vehicle, in meters.
leadVehicleVelocity The lead vehicle's velocity along our travel axis, in m/s.
nosZones List of active NOS zones the vehicle is currently inside.
obstaclesLayerMask The layer mask used for obstacle detection.
pathAdvanceDistance The resolved path advancement distance for the current frame.
pathCurrentPointIndex The current index of the path point being targeted.
pathStartPointIndex The index of the starting point on the path.
pathSteeringInput The steering input resolved from the path alone, before obstacle avoidance.
pathWidthMultiplier Multiplier for how far from the center of the path the vehicle can drive (0 = center, 1 = edge).
recoveryAttemptCount The number of recovery attempts made, escalating the timeouts of each successive attempt.
recoveryResetCount How many path resets have been performed at the same trapped position. Each successive one lands further along the path, since landing on the same blocked stretch again solved nothing.
recoveryResumeTimer Counts down after a recovery; surviving it without getting stuck again resets the escalation.
recoveryStartPosition The position the vehicle started the current reverse manoeuvre from.
recoveryState The current stage of the stuck detection and reverse recovery manoeuvre.
recoveryStuckTimer How long the vehicle has continuously satisfied the stuck test, in seconds.
recoveryTimer How long the current reverse manoeuvre has been running, in seconds.
recoveryTrapAttempts How many recovery attempts have started near the same trapped position.
recoveryTrapPosition Where the vehicle was when its recovery attempts started piling up. Attempts that begin near this position count towards the reset; getting away from it starts the count over.
sensorCommands The raycast commands issued for the current update, kept for gizmo drawing.
sensorMinimumRange The shortest the front sensors ever reach, in meters. Zero resolves to the vehicle length.
sensorRange The sensor range for the current update, in meters.
sensorSamples The resolved reading of each obstacle sensor for the current update.
sensorTimeHeadway How many seconds ahead the front sensors reach at the current speed.
sensorsBrakeInput The brake input from sensors (obstacle avoidance).
sensorsIntensityPower Power factor for how sensor intensity is calculated.
sensorsMaximumHits The maximum number of hits to check for each sensor raycast.
sensorsSteeringInput The steering input from sensors (obstacle avoidance).
sensorsSteeringInputIntensity The intensity of steering input from sensors (obstacle avoidance).
sideSensorsSteerIntensity Steering intensity for side sensors.
stabilityFrontLateralInfluence How much the front axle's lateral grip counts towards limiting the brakes, relative to the rear. A saturated rear risks a spin, so it dominates; a saturated front only understeers, where scrubbing speed off is the right answer.
stabilityMinimumBrakeCeiling The least brake the stability limit will ever leave available, so the vehicle can still slow down while sliding.
startPoint How to select the starting point on the path.
steeringPathPointIndex The current path point index used for lookahead steering.
steeringTargetPointPosition The resolved world target used by the steering controller.
targetSpeedMultiplier Multiplier for the corner target speeds (1 = normal, <1 = slower, >1 = faster). Values below one also cap the vehicle's overall speed to that fraction of its top speed, so a traffic vehicle stays slow on straights too; values above one only raise corner speeds.
useRecoveryReset Whether the vehicle may teleport back onto its path once every reverse recovery attempt at the same spot has failed. Without it, a physically wedged vehicle retries forever.
vehicleCenter The center of the vehicle's bounding box (local space).
vehicleCurbWeight The curb weight of the vehicle.
vehicleExtents The extents of the vehicle's bounding box (local space).
vehicleInstance Reference to the controlled vehicle instance.
vehicleLength The vehicle's length, used as the sensor minimum range when it is not overridden.
vehiclePeakPower The vehicle's peak engine power in horsepower. Independent of the current throttle.
vehiclePivotPoint The pivot point of the vehicle (usually front wheels position).
vehicleTopVelocity The top velocity of the vehicle (in m/s).
zonesBrakeInput The brake input from zones (brake zones).
zonesHandbrakeInput The handbrake input from zones (handbrake zones).
zonesNOSInput Whether the vehicle should use NOS (from zone).

ApplyPedals(MVC.Core.Vehicle.InputsAccess@) Calculates and applies throttle, brake, handbrake, and NOS inputs based on path, sensors, zones, and traffic.
ApplySteering(MVC.Core.Vehicle.InputsAccess@) Calculates and applies steering input based on the path, obstacle sensors, and recovery state.

OnActivation Reacquires the closest path point when this behaviour resumes after player control. A configured path start remains authoritative for .

OnStart Initializes the AI path follower, setting up references, zones, and coefficients. Called when the AI behaviour is started or when the path/follow direction changes.
OnTriggerEnter(UnityEngine.Collider) Handles trigger entry events for AI zones (brake, handbrake, NOS). Adds the zone to the appropriate list if not already present.
OnTriggerExit(UnityEngine.Collider) Handles trigger exit events for AI zones (brake, handbrake, NOS). Removes the zone from the appropriate list.
OnUpdate(MVC.Core.Vehicle.InputsAccess@) Main update loop for the AI path follower. Handles path progress, obstacle detection, zone logic, traffic, recovery, steering, and input calculation.
PerformRecoveryReset(System.Int32) Puts the vehicle back onto its path, upright and stationary, facing along the follow direction. The last resort once driving out of a stuck spot has repeatedly failed. Each successive reset at the same trap lands further along the path, because landing on the same blocked stretch of road again would just repeat the trap.
RefreshCoefficients Refreshes all cached vehicle and path coefficients used for AI calculations. Should be called whenever the vehicle or path changes.
ResolveActiveZone(System.Collections.Generic.List{MVC.AI.VehicleAIZone}) Returns the first still-valid zone of a list, dropping any that were destroyed while inside.
ResolveApproachVelocityLimit(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the highest velocity the vehicle can hold now and still slow to a corner's velocity by the time it arrives.
ResolveAvoidanceBlend(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Blends the path steering with the obstacle avoidance steering. The blend is clamped, so it can never extrapolate past either input.
ResolveCornerVelocity(MVC.Utilities.CurvePoint, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves a path point's cornering velocity, in m/s, clamped into a usable range. A straight has no curvature and would otherwise evaluate to infinity.
ResolveCornerVelocityLimit Scans the path ahead and returns the highest velocity the vehicle can hold and still make every upcoming corner.
ResolveDiagonalAngleFactor(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves how narrow the diagonal sensors currently are, from 0 at their widest to 1 at their narrowest.
ResolveDiagonalSensorsAngle(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the spread of the diagonal sensors at a given velocity, in degrees. The sensors fan out at a standstill and narrow towards the reference velocity.
ResolveDiagonalSteerIntensity(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPathFollower.SensorSample) Resolves the steer intensity a diagonal sensor should apply, honouring the traffic policy. Traffic queues in lane rather than swerving around other vehicles; Racing passes them.
ResolveFollowVelocityLimit(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the velocity cap needed to keep a gap behind a lead vehicle, in m/s. At exactly the desired gap this returns the lead's velocity, which settles into speed matching.
ResolveGripUtilization(System.Single, System.Single) Resolves how much of an axle's lateral grip is currently spent, where 1 means it is exactly at the slip its tyres make peak grip at, and beyond 1 means it is sliding.
ResolveLookAheadDistance(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves how far ahead of the vehicle the steering controller should aim, in meters.
ResolveLookAheadPointIndex(System.Int32, System.Int32, System.Int32, System.Boolean, MVC.AI.VehicleAIPathFollower.FollowDirection) Offsets a path point index along the follow direction, wrapping on looped paths and clamping otherwise. A negative offset walks backwards along the direction of travel.
ResolveLookAheadPointOffset(System.Single, System.Single) Converts a look ahead distance into a number of spaced path points.
ResolvePathPointTarget(MVC.Utilities.CurvePoint, Unity.Mathematics.float3, System.Single) Resolves the world position on a path point's width band that the vehicle should aim at.
ResolvePedalControlDistance(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the distance the pedal controller plans its acceleration over, never collapsing to zero.
ResolvePedalTargets(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Boolean) Resolves the pedal demands needed to reach a target velocity over a control distance.
ResolvePurePursuitSteeringInput(Unity.Mathematics.float3, Unity.Mathematics.float3, Unity.Mathematics.float3, Unity.Mathematics.float3, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the steering input that steers the vehicle onto a target point, using the pure pursuit model.
ResolveRecoverySteeringInput Resolves the steering input for a reverse recovery, aiming the rear of the vehicle back down the path.
ResolveSensorBrakeInput(MVC.AI.VehicleAIPathFollower.SensorSample, System.Single) Resolves the emergency brake demand of the front sensor. A dynamic obstacle is braked for in proportion to how fast we are closing on it, so one pulling away is not braked for.
ResolveSensorRange(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves how far the front sensors reach at a given velocity, in meters.
ResolveSensorSample(Unity.Collections.NativeArray{UnityEngine.RaycastHit}, System.Int32, System.Single, Unity.Mathematics.float3) Resolves the closest valid hit of a single sensor from the batched results.
ResolveStabilityBrakeCeiling(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the most brake the vehicle can take without losing grip. A tyre has one grip budget to spend across cornering and braking, so whatever is already being spent holding the vehicle through a corner is not available to stop it. Braking past that is how an AI puts itself off the road.
ResolveStabilityFuelCeiling(System.Single, System.Single) Resolves the most throttle the vehicle can take without spinning up its driven wheels, from 0 to 1. Only the rear axle counts: drive torque on a rear axle that is already saturated sideways is what turns a fast corner into a spin, while a saturated front axle merely pushes wide.

VehicleAITargetFollower
VehicleAITargetFollower is an AI behaviour for vehicles that enables them to follow a moving or static target using Unity's NavMeshAgent. This class manages the creation and configuration of a NavMeshAgent for the vehicle, allowing it to navigate the environment, avoid obstacles, and follow a target dynamically. It is intended for use in scenarios where the vehicle must pursue a target rather than follow a predefined path.
Fields
Name Description
agent The NavMeshAgent component responsible for navigation and obstacle avoidance.
agentTypeID The agent type ID used by the NavMeshAgent. Determines which NavMesh the agent will use.
obstacleAvoidanceType The obstacle avoidance type for the NavMeshAgent. Controls how the agent avoids obstacles.
vehicleInstance Reference to the vehicle instance controlled by this AI.
Methods
Name Description
Initialize Destroys the current NavMeshAgent and its GameObject, if present. Used to clean up the agent before reinitialization or destruction.
OnUpdate(MVC.Core.Vehicle.InputsAccess@) Updates the AI's input values each frame. This method should be extended to implement target following logic and set the vehicle's inputs accordingly.
Restart Restarts the AI behaviour, initializing or recreating the NavMeshAgent as needed. Sets up the agent's parameters to match the vehicle's dimensions and configures navigation settings.
Initialize
Destroys the current NavMeshAgent and its GameObject, if present. Used to clean up the agent before reinitialization or destruction.

Updates the AI's input values each frame. This method should be extended to implement target following logic and set the vehicle's inputs accordingly.

VehicleAIZone
VehicleAIZone defines a special zone along a VehicleAIPath that modifies AI vehicle behavior. Zones can be of type Brake, Handbrake, or NOS, and each type applies specific input modifications (such as braking intensity, speed targets, slip, or NOS minimums) to vehicles that enter the zone. This class exposes properties for configuring the effect of the zone and provides editor visualization. Check the class for more information.
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-ai-vehicleaizone-aizonetype](AIZoneType) The type of AI zone, determining which vehicle input is affected.
Fields
Name Description
brakeSpeedTarget The serialized target speed for braking zones.
brakingIntensity The serialized braking intensity for braking zones.
handbrakeSlipTarget The serialized slip target for handbrake zones.
minimumNOSTarget The serialized minimum NOS value for NOS zones.
snapBrakeSpeedTarget If true, the AI will snap to the brake speed target instantly when entering the zone. If false, the AI may approach the target speed more gradually.
zoneType The type of this AI zone (Brake, Handbrake, or NOS). Determines which vehicle input is affected when inside this zone.
Methods
Name Description
OnDrawGizmosSelected Draws gizmos in the Unity Editor to visualize the zone when it is selected. The gizmo color is determined by the zone type for easy identification.
AIZoneType
The type of AI zone, determining which vehicle input is affected.
Fields
Name Description
Brake Zone that applies braking to the vehicle.
Handbrake Zone that applies handbrake (drift/slip) to the vehicle.
NOS Zone that applies a minimum NOS (nitrous) value to the vehicle.
Base
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-base-ivehiclephysicsintegration](IVehiclePhysicsIntegration) Describes a wheel physics integration available to the toolkit. Implementations are discovered automatically from any loaded assembly through reflection ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â implementing this interface on a non-abstract class with a parameterless constructor is all that is required to register a new physics backend.
[#mvc-base-pacejkacurvefitutility](PacejkaCurveFitUtility) Fits Pacejka Magic Formula coefficients from Unity-style slip friction curves (extremum/asymptote points), so existing tire compounds work with Pacejka-based physics integrations without manual re-tuning.
[#mvc-base-unitywheelcolliderbackend](UnityWheelColliderBackend) The built-in wheel backend wrapping Unity's . Reproduces the toolkit's historical behavior exactly and keeps assigned for backwards compatibility.
[#mvc-base-unitywheelcolliderintegration](UnityWheelColliderIntegration) The built-in Unity WheelCollider physics integration. Always available; acts as the default and fallback integration for the toolkit.
[#mvc-base-unitywheelcollidersettings](UnityWheelColliderSettings) Settings for Unity's WheelCollider integration.
[#mvc-base-vehicleantiswayapplication](VehicleAntiSwayApplication) Selects how MVC applies anti-sway-bar loads for an integration.
[#mvc-base-vehicleaudiozone](VehicleAudioZone) VehicleAudioZone is a specialized zone for handling audio effects in the vehicle system. This class extends to provide support for spatial audio zones, such as reverb, that dynamically adjust their parameters based on the zone's geometry and the listener's position. The main use case is to automatically manage an component, updating its min/max distances to match the zone's collider and the listener's proximity.
[#mvc-base-vehiclecharger](VehicleCharger) Represents a charger component that can be attached to a vehicle and configured to be compatible with specific engines. Provides methods to manage the list of compatible engines, including adding, removing, and resetting compatibility. Also handles validation and updates of engine-related properties such as mass and RPM ranges.
[#mvc-base-vehiclechargeraccess](VehicleChargerAccess) Provides native array access to VehicleCharger data for high-performance operations. This struct is designed for use with Unity's Job System and Burst compiler. Implements IDisposable to properly manage native memory allocation.
[#mvc-base-vehicledamagezone](VehicleDamageZone) Represents a specific damage zone on a vehicle, such as a repair area or a wheel. This component is used to define areas on the vehicle that can be damaged or repaired, and provides visualization in the Unity Editor using gizmos. Inherits from .
[#mvc-base-vehicleengine](VehicleEngine) Represents the core logic and utility functions for a vehicle engine within the MVC framework.
[#mvc-base-vehicleengineaccess](VehicleEngineAccess) Provides read-only access to VehicleEngine parameters for efficient data transfer and external system integration. This struct is designed for performance-critical operations and is marked as readonly for thread safety.
[#mvc-base-vehicleexhaust](VehicleExhaust) Represents an exhaust component for a vehicle within the MVC framework.
[#mvc-base-vehiclefollowerpivot](VehicleFollowerPivot) VehicleFollowerPivot represents a pivot point for a camera to follow a vehicle. It manages the association between a pivot and a specific camera index, and provides information about whether the pivot is inside the vehicle. This class is intended to be attached to GameObjects that serve as camera pivots in the Multiversal Vehicle Controller system.
[#mvc-base-vehiclefollowerpivotaccess](VehicleFollowerPivotAccess) VehicleFollowerPivotAccess is a lightweight, readonly struct used to provide fast, value-type access to the essential data of a VehicleFollowerPivot for jobs and native operations.
[#mvc-base-vehiclelight](VehicleLight) Represents a single light component on a vehicle, such as a headlight, rear light, or indicator. Handles light state, emission, dynamic positioning, and light source management.
[#mvc-base-vehiclelightsource](VehicleLightSource) Manages individual light sources for vehicles, handling light intensity, technology types, and state management. This component works in conjunction with VehicleLight to provide realistic lighting behavior including high beam logic, engine start flickering, and different technology responses (Lamp vs LED).
[#mvc-base-vehiclephysicsintegrationcapabilities](VehiclePhysicsIntegrationCapabilities) Runtime behaviors that materially differ between wheel integrations.
[#mvc-base-vehiclephysicsintegrationregistry](VehiclePhysicsIntegrationRegistry) Discovers and exposes the wheel physics integrations available to the toolkit. Any non-abstract implementation with a parameterless constructor found in a loaded assembly is registered automatically. In the community version, pluggable integrations are unavailable: the registry is hard-wired to the built-in and performs no type discovery at all.
[#mvc-base-vehiclephysicsintegrationsettings](VehiclePhysicsIntegrationSettings) Base type for integration-owned, globally serialized settings.
[#mvc-base-vehiclephysicsintegrationsettingsentry](VehiclePhysicsIntegrationSettingsEntry) Serialized stable-name association for an integration's typed settings.
[#mvc-base-vehicletirecompound](VehicleTireCompound) Represents a tire compound configuration for a vehicle, encapsulating how tire friction and slip characteristics are affected by tire width and wetness. This class provides methods to calculate the effective tire stiffness based on these parameters and validates the configuration for correctness.
[#mvc-base-vehicletrailer](VehicleTrailer) Represents a trailer vehicle that can be attached to other vehicles. This class handles the core trailer functionality including physics, joints, and behavior.
[#mvc-base-vehicleweatherzone](VehicleWeatherZone) Represents a weather zone that affects vehicle behavior and rendering. This component creates environmental effects like darkness or fog within a defined area. Inherits from VehicleZone to provide zone-based functionality.
[#mvc-base-vehiclewheelcolliderbase](VehicleWheelColliderBase) Abstract wheel-collider backend owned by a single . Implementations bridge MVC's wheel model to a concrete physics simulation (Unity's WheelCollider, the Pacejka Wheel Collider, or future integrations).
[#mvc-base-vehiclewheelcolliderconfig](VehicleWheelColliderConfig) Backend-neutral per-wheel physical configuration, flushed to the active each physics step. Implementations perform their own change detection before writing to the underlying physics objects.
[#mvc-base-vehiclewheelfrictionstate](VehicleWheelFrictionState) Backend-neutral tire friction state for a single direction (forward or sideways), composed by each physics step from the active tire compound, drift blending, and ground/wetness/width stiffness modifiers.
[#mvc-base-vehiclewheelhit](VehicleWheelHit) Backend-neutral wheel ground-hit information, replacing across the toolkit. Populated by the active implementation each physics step.
[#mvc-base-vehiclezone](VehicleZone) VehicleZone is a base class for defining spatial zones in the vehicle system. Zones can be used to trigger or modify vehicle behavior (AI, audio, damage, weather, etc.) when a vehicle enters or interacts with them. This class manages the zone's collider (box or sphere), its type, and provides utility methods for collider management and editor visualization.
[#mvc-base-vehiclezonescontainer](VehicleZonesContainer) Container component that manages and creates various types of vehicle zones. This component serves as a parent container for organizing different zone types such as AI zones, audio zones, damage zones, and weather zones.

VehicleAudioZone
VehicleAudioZone is a specialized zone for handling audio effects in the vehicle system. This class extends to provide support for spatial audio zones, such as reverb, that dynamically adjust their parameters based on the zone's geometry and the listener's position. The main use case is to automatically manage an component, updating its min/max distances to match the zone's collider and the listener's proximity.
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-base-vehicleaudiozone-audiozonetype](AudioZoneType) The type of audio zone effect this zone provides. Currently only Reverb is supported, but this can be extended in the future.
Fields
Name Description
maxZoneDistanceMultiplier The multiplier used to expand the max distance of the audio zone relative to its minimum distance. Default is 1.25.
reverbZone The cached reference to the component. This is managed automatically by the property.
zoneType The type of audio effect this zone provides (e.g., Reverb).
Methods
Name Description
Awake Unity Awake callback. Ensures the zone is initialized and ready.
FarthestPointInBox(UnityEngine.Vector3, UnityEngine.Vector3, UnityEngine.Vector3, UnityEngine.Quaternion) Returns a point on an oriented box in the local direction of a world-space query point.
LateUpdate Unity LateUpdate callback. Ensures the audio zone's size is kept up to date every frame while the zone is active.
OnDrawGizmosSelected Draws gizmos in the editor to visualize the audio zone when it is selected. The gizmo color is set according to the audio reverb zone settings.
RefreshZoneSize Updates the 's minDistance and maxDistance properties to match the current zone's geometry and the listener's position. For box zones, the minimum distance is calculated as the distance from the reverb zone's center to the closest point on the box collider to the listener. For sphere zones, it is the sphere's radius. The maximum distance is determined by multiplying the minimum distance by .
Restart Restarts the audio zone, re-initializing its state and refreshing its size. This should be called after any significant change to the zone's configuration.

Front Engine located at the front of the vehicle, typically front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive.

Name Description

Electric Electric motor configuration with no internal combustion.
Inline Inline engine configuration with cylinders arranged in a straight line.

V V-engine configuration with cylinders arranged in a V-shape.
W W-engine configuration with cylinders arranged in a W-shape (typically three banks).

Editor-only. Moves the dynamic transform to its dynamic target pose so the light can be previewed in its deployed position (e.g. while editing its emission). The resting pose is captured first so can revert it. No-op in Play Mode, when already applied, or when the light isn't Dynamic with a valid transform.
Emission
Updates the emission state of the light, either by material color or by enabling/disabling GameObjects.
GetDynamicTargetLocalPosition
Gets the deployed local position for a dynamic light, falling back to its captured resting position.
Returns The target local position used by dynamic interpolation.
GetDynamicTargetLocalRotation
Gets the deployed local rotation for a dynamic light, falling back to its captured resting rotation.
Returns The target local rotation used by dynamic interpolation.
GetLightSource

Returns The VehicleLightSource, or null if none.
GetLightSourceName
Gets a valid GameObject name for the light source (no spaces).
Returns Light source name string.
GetMaterialEmissionColorPropertyName
Gets the property name for emission color in the material, based on shader.
Returns Property name string, or empty if not found.
GetName

GetRuntimeEmissionMaterial
Returns the runtime material instance used for light emission, creating it once if needed.
GetSourcePosition
Gets the world position of the light source.
Returns World position, or Vector3.zero if no source.
GetTypeName
Gets a human-readable type name for this light.
Returns Type name string.
Initialize
Resets internal state and references for this light.
IsOverriddenByHigherPriorityHighBeam
Returns true when this low beam should remain off because a higher-priority high beam is active on the same renderer slot.
Returns True when a matching high beam overrides this low beam; otherwise false.
PositionAndRotation
Updates the position and rotation of the light if dynamic, interpolating as needed.
RefreshMaterialEmissionColorPropertyName
Forces the emission color property name to be refreshed on next access.
RemoveLightSource
Removes and destroys the light source GameObject.
Restart
Initializes or re-initializes the light, setting up references, state, and emission.
RestoreDynamicEditorPreview
Editor-only. Restores the dynamic transform to the resting pose captured by . No-op if no preview pose is currently applied.
Source
Updates the light source component, if present.
State
Updates the logical state (on/off) of the light based on vehicle stats and light type.
Update
Updates the state, position, emission, and source of the light for the current frame.
UpdateParent
Updates the parent transform for the dynamic transform, adjusting local position/rotation if needed.

VehicleTireCompound
Represents a tire compound configuration for a vehicle, encapsulating how tire friction and slip characteristics are affected by tire width and wetness. This class provides methods to calculate the effective tire stiffness based on these parameters and validates the configuration for correctness.
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-base-vehicletirecompound-frictioncomplexity](FrictionComplexity) Defines the complexity level for friction calculations in wheel collider friction curves. Determines whether to use simple constant values or complex speed-dependent calculations.
[#mvc-base-vehicletirecompound-pacejkafrictioncurve](PacejkaFrictionCurve) A Pacejka Magic Formula friction curve owned by the toolkit, consumed by physics integrations that simulate tire friction with Pacejka coefficients. Mirrors the formula `DÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·sin(CÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·atan(BÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·kÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·slip ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ EÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·(BÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·kÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·slip ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ atan(BÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·kÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·slip))))` without depending on any integration package.
[#mvc-base-vehicletirecompound-pacejkasource](PacejkaSource) Determines how a tire compound's Pacejka coefficients are obtained.
[#mvc-base-vehicletirecompound-wheelcolliderfrictioncurve](WheelColliderFrictionCurve) Represents a friction curve configuration for wheel colliders, defining how tire friction behaves under different slip conditions and speeds. Used for acceleration, braking, and sideways friction.
[#mvc-base-vehicletirecompound-widthfrictionmodifier](WidthFrictionModifier) Defines how tire width affects friction characteristics. Wider tires generally provide better grip due to increased contact patch area. This struct allows fine-tuning of friction multipliers based on specific tire widths.
Fields
Name Description
frictionComplexity Determines the overall complexity of friction calculations for this tire compound. Affects performance and realism of tire behavior across all friction curves.
isValid Internal cache for the validity state of the tire compound. Prevents repeated validation calculations when accessed multiple times.
name The internal name field for the tire compound. Used by the Name property to store the actual name value.
pacejkaAccelerationFriction The Pacejka representation of . Fitted automatically unless its source is set to manual.
pacejkaBrakeFriction The Pacejka representation of . Fitted automatically unless its source is set to manual.
pacejkaSidewaysFriction The Pacejka representation of . Fitted automatically unless its source is set to manual.
wetFrictionMultiplier Multiplier applied to friction values when driving on wet surfaces. Values less than 1.0 reduce grip in wet conditions for realistic behavior.
wetSlipMultiplier Multiplier applied to slip thresholds when driving on wet surfaces. Values greater than 1.0 increase the slip angle at which grip is lost.
wheelColliderAccelerationFriction Friction curve configuration for acceleration scenarios. Defines how the tire behaves when applying power to the wheels. Optimized for forward traction and launch characteristics.
wheelColliderBrakeFriction Friction curve configuration for braking scenarios. Defines how the tire behaves when applying braking force to the wheels. Optimized for stopping power and brake feel.
wheelColliderSidewaysFriction Friction curve configuration for lateral (sideways) movement. Defines how the tire behaves during cornering and side-to-side movement. Critical for handling characteristics and cornering stability.
widthFrictionModifiers Array of width-based friction modifiers that adjust tire performance based on tire width. Wider tires generally provide better grip due to increased contact patch area.
Methods
Name Description
GetStiffness(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single) Calculates the effective tire stiffness for a given set of parameters. The stiffness is determined by the base friction curve stiffness, a width-dependent multiplier, and a wetness-dependent multiplier.
RefreshPacejkaFits Re-fits every Pacejka curve whose source is from the compound's slip friction curves. Manual curves are left untouched.
RefreshValidity Validates the configuration of the tire compound, ensuring that: - The widthFrictionModifiers array is sorted by width in ascending order. - The wetFrictionMultiplier and wetSlipMultiplier are non-negative. Sets the field accordingly.
GetStiffness(System.Single, System.Single, System.Single)
Calculates the effective tire stiffness for a given set of parameters. The stiffness is determined by the base friction curve stiffness, a width-dependent multiplier, and a wetness-dependent multiplier.
Returns The calculated effective tire stiffness, factoring in width and wetness multipliers.
Parameter Type Description
System.Single The base friction curve stiffness value for the tire.
System.Single The width of the tire, used to determine the width friction modifier.
System.Single A value between 0 (dry) and 1 (fully wet) representing the wetness of the surface.
RefreshPacejkaFits
Re-fits every Pacejka curve whose source is from the compound's slip friction curves. Manual curves are left untouched.
RefreshValidity
Validates the configuration of the tire compound, ensuring that: - The widthFrictionModifiers array is sorted by width in ascending order. - The wetFrictionMultiplier and wetSlipMultiplier are non-negative. Sets the field accordingly.

FrictionComplexity
Defines the complexity level for friction calculations in wheel collider friction curves. Determines whether to use simple constant values or complex speed-dependent calculations.
Fields
Name Description
Complex Complex friction calculation using speed-dependent stiffness intervals. Offers more realistic tire behavior but requires additional computation.
Simple Simple friction calculation using constant stiffness values. Provides basic performance with minimal computational overhead.
PacejkaFrictionCurve
A Pacejka Magic Formula friction curve owned by the toolkit, consumed by physics integrations that simulate tire friction with Pacejka coefficients. Mirrors the formula `DÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·sin(CÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·atan(BÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·kÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·slip ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ EÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·(BÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·kÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·slip ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ atan(BÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·kÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·slip))))` without depending on any integration package.
Fields
Name Description
b Curve stiffness; controls the slope at small slip values. Range in [1, 100].
c Curve shape factor. Range in [1, 2].
d Curve peak grip multiplier.
e Curvature factor, adjusts the shape near the peak. Range in [0, 1].
slipMultiplier Slip stiffness multiplier, scales the effective slip fed to the curve.
source How the coefficients of this curve are obtained.
Methods
Name Description
Evaluate(System.Single) Evaluates the Magic Formula at a given slip value.
EvaluatePeakSlip(System.Int32) Approximates the slip value at which the curve reaches peak grip by sampling.

Evaluates the Magic Formula at a given slip value.
Returns The friction multiplier. Range in [-d, d].
Parameter Type Description
System.Single The slip value (ratio or radians, direction-dependent).
EvaluatePeakSlip(System.Int32)
Approximates the slip value at which the curve reaches peak grip by sampling.
Returns The peak slip value.
Parameter Type Description
System.Int32 The number of samples across [0, 1] slip.
PacejkaSource
Determines how a tire compound's Pacejka coefficients are obtained.
Fields
Name Description
FitFromSlipCurve Coefficients are fitted automatically from the compound's slip friction curve.
Manual Coefficients are authored manually.
WheelColliderFrictionCurve
Represents a friction curve configuration for wheel colliders, defining how tire friction behaves under different slip conditions and speeds. Used for acceleration, braking, and sideways friction.
Fields
Name Description
asymptoteSlip The slip value beyond which friction begins to decrease significantly. Represents the point where the tire starts to lose grip.
asymptoteValue The minimum friction value that the curve approaches at high slip angles. Represents the residual grip when the tire is severely oversteering.
extremumSlip The slip value at which the friction curve reaches its maximum (peak) value. Represents the optimal slip angle for maximum grip.
extremumValue The maximum friction value achieved at the extremum slip point. This is the peak grip level of the tire.
stiffness The base stiffness value for the friction curve. Higher values create more responsive but potentially unstable behavior.
stiffnessComplexity Determines the complexity of stiffness calculations. Simple mode uses constant values, Complex mode uses speed-dependent intervals.
stiffnessInterval The range of stiffness values when using complex friction calculations. Allows stiffness to vary based on vehicle speed for more realistic behavior.
stiffnessSpeedInterval The speed range over which stiffness interpolation occurs. Defines the minimum and maximum speeds for stiffness variation.
Methods
Name Description
GetStiffness(System.Single) Calculates the effective stiffness value based on the current vehicle speed. Uses complex interpolation when stiffnessComplexity is set to Complex, otherwise returns the constant stiffness value.
GetStiffness(System.Single)
Calculates the effective stiffness value based on the current vehicle speed. Uses complex interpolation when stiffnessComplexity is set to Complex, otherwise returns the constant stiffness value.
Returns The calculated stiffness value for the current speed.
Parameter Type Description
System.Single The current vehicle speed in appropriate units.
WidthFrictionModifier
Defines how tire width affects friction characteristics. Wider tires generally provide better grip due to increased contact patch area. This struct allows fine-tuning of friction multipliers based on specific tire widths.
Fields
Name Description
frictionMultiplier The friction multiplier applied to tires of the specified width. Values greater than 1.0 increase friction, values less than 1.0 decrease friction. Must be a positive value to maintain realistic physics behavior.
width The tire width in millimeters that this modifier applies to. Must be a positive value representing the actual tire width.

Initializes a new width friction modifier with specified width and friction multiplier.
Parameter Type Description
System.Int32 The tire width in millimeters.
System.Single The friction multiplier for this width.
VehicleTrailer
Represents a trailer vehicle that can be attached to other vehicles. This class handles the core trailer functionality including physics, joints, and behavior.
Types
Name Description
[#mvc-base-vehicletrailer-behaviourmodule](BehaviourModule) Module responsible for controlling the behavioral aspects of the trailer. Handles weight distribution, physics behavior, and other behavioral parameters.
[#mvc-base-vehicletrailer-componentsmodule](ComponentsModule) Module responsible for managing the core components and references of the trailer. Handles vehicle connections and component validation.
[#mvc-base-vehicletrailer-followermodifieraccess](FollowerModifierAccess) Internal struct that provides read-only access to follower modifier values. Used to safely expose follower modifier data without allowing external modification.
[#mvc-base-vehicletrailer-followermodifiermodule](FollowerModifierModule) Module responsible for controlling how the trailer follows the lead vehicle. Handles distance and height offsets to create realistic following behavior.
[#mvc-base-vehicletrailer-jointmodule](JointModule) Module responsible for managing the physical joint connection between the trailer and vehicle. Handles joint positioning, rotation limits, break forces, and vehicle connections.
Fields
Name Description
LINK_COLLISION_SETTLE_FIXED_STEPS Number of fixed steps to suppress truck/trailer body collisions while a new link settles.
detectedLink Temporary variable storing the detected trailer link during connection attempts. Used to track potential connection targets before establishing the actual joint.
followerModifier The serialized follower modifier module instance for controlling following behavior. Manages distance and height offsets when following a lead vehicle.
ignoredTrailerColliders Colliders on this trailer whose collisions are ignored while the link settles.
ignoredVehicleColliders Colliders on the connected vehicle whose collisions are ignored while the link settles.
joint The serialized joint module instance for managing trailer-vehicle connections. Handles all aspects of the physical joint including positioning and limits.
linkCollisionSettleSteps Remaining fixed steps before normal truck/trailer body collisions are restored.
linkHits Temporary array for storing collision detection results during link detection. Used to find potential trailer links in the vicinity.
linkJoint Temporary reference to the configurable joint component used for trailer connection. Created dynamically when connecting to a vehicle and destroyed on disconnection.
linkJustBroke Temporary reference to a trailer link that just broke/disconnected. Used to handle cleanup and state management after joint failure.
solverSettingsBody Rigidbody whose solver settings were temporarily boosted while linked.
stands The serialized transform reference for the trailer's support stands. Must be a child of the trailer's chassis for proper functionality.
standsIdleLocalPosition The serialized idle (resting) local position of the trailer stands. Represents the stands' location when fully deployed and supporting the trailer.
standsIdleLocalRotation The serialized idle (resting) local rotation of the trailer stands. Represents the stands' position when fully deployed and supporting the trailer.
standsLiftPositionFactor Temporary factor for calculating the lift position of trailer stands. Used during stand deployment/retraction animations.
standsLiftRotationFactor Temporary factor for calculating the lift rotation of trailer stands. Used during stand deployment/retraction animations.
standsLiftTime The serialized time duration for stand deployment/retraction animations in seconds. Default value is 2 seconds for smooth, realistic stand movement.
standsLiftedLocalPosition The serialized lifted (retracted) local position of the trailer stands. Represents the stands' location when fully retracted during transport.
standsLiftedLocalRotation The serialized lifted (retracted) local rotation of the trailer stands. Represents the stands' position when fully retracted during transport.
trailerBehaviour The serialized behavior module instance for controlling trailer physics behavior. Overrides the base vehicle behavior with trailer-specific parameters.
trailerBrakes The serialized brake module instance for controlling trailer braking. Only active when useBrakes is enabled.
useBrakes Flag that determines whether the trailer should use its own braking system. When enabled, the trailer will have independent brake control. When disabled, braking is handled entirely by the connected vehicle.

JointModule
Module responsible for managing the physical joint connection between the trailer and vehicle. Handles joint positioning, rotation limits, break forces, and vehicle connections.
Fields
Name Description
angularMotionXLimit The angular motion limits for the X-axis rotation in degrees. Defines the range of motion for pitch (forward/backward tilt). Default range is -30 to +30 degrees.
breakForce The serialized break force threshold in Newtons. Default value is infinity, meaning the joint will never break from force.
breakTorque The serialized break torque threshold in Newton-meters. Default value is infinity, meaning the joint will never break from torque.
connectedVehicle Cached reference to the connected vehicle for performance optimization. Automatically updated when the ConnectedLink changes.
jointRotationAxis The serialized rotation axis for the joint's angular motion. Defaults to Vector3.up (Y-axis) for typical trailer rotation behavior.
position The serialized local position of the joint connection point. Represents where the trailer connects to the vehicle in local coordinates.

Backend-neutral per-wheel physical configuration, flushed to the active each physics step. Implementations perform their own change detection before writing to the underlying physics objects.
Fields
Name Description
baseRadius The undamaged base wheel radius (in meters), used for collider placement.
camber The camber alignment angle (in degrees).
caster The caster alignment angle (in degrees).
forceAppPointDistance The distance from the contact point at which tire forces are applied (in meters).
layer The layer assigned to the wheel's collider GameObject.
mass The wheel mass (in kilograms).
radius The current effective wheel radius (in meters), accounting for tire wear.
sideOffset The sideways offset of the wheel from its anchor (in meters). Zero when side offsets are visual-only or suspension adjustments are disabled.
springDamper The suspension damper rate (in Newton-seconds per meter).
springStiffness The suspension spring rate (in Newtons per meter).
springTargetPosition The suspension rest position within the travel range, normalized to [0, 1].
suspensionDistance The maximum suspension travel distance (in meters), stance-adjusted.
suspensionLength The raw suspension length (in meters) without stance adjustment, used for collider placement.
toe The toe alignment angle (in degrees).
toeAngle The wheel's current signed toe angle (in degrees), including the wheel-side sign.

VehicleWheelFrictionState
Backend-neutral tire friction state for a single direction (forward or sideways), composed by each physics step from the active tire compound, drift blending, and ground/wetness/width stiffness modifiers.
Fields
Name Description
asymptoteSlip The slip value at which grip settles to its asymptote.
asymptoteValue The grip multiplier past the asymptote slip point.
extremumSlip The slip value at which the tire reaches peak grip.
extremumValue The grip multiplier at the extremum slip point.
hasPacejka True when carries valid coefficients.
pacejka The Pacejka representation of this friction state, for integrations that consume Magic Formula coefficients. Only meaningful when is true.
stiffness The final composite stiffness multiplier (speed, width, wetness, drift and ABS/ground multipliers already applied).
VehicleWheelHit
Backend-neutral wheel ground-hit information, replacing across the toolkit. Populated by the active implementation each physics step.
Fields
Name Description
collider The collider that was hit, if the active backend can provide it. May be null (e.g. the Pacejka hybrid backend) â€” consumers must null-check before use.
force The magnitude of the suspension force pushing against the ground (in Newtons).
forwardDir The direction the wheel is rolling in, in world space.
forwardSlip Tire slip in the rolling direction, expressed in MVC's legacy Unity-compatible units.
nativeForwardPeakSlip Forward peak slip in the active integration's native units.
nativeForwardSlip Forward slip in the active integration's native units.
nativeSidewaysPeakSlip Sideways peak slip in the active integration's native units.
nativeSidewaysSlip Sideways slip in the active integration's native units.
normal The normal of the ground surface at the point of contact, in world space.
normalizedForwardSlip Absolute forward slip divided by the backend's forward peak (extremum) slip. Values above 1 mean the tire has exceeded its grip peak. Unit-free across backends.
normalizedSidewaysSlip Absolute sideways slip divided by the backend's sideways peak (extremum) slip. Values above 1 mean the tire has exceeded its grip peak. Unit-free across backends.
point The point of contact between the wheel and the ground, in world space.
sidewaysDir The sideways direction of the wheel, in world space.
sidewaysSlip Tire slip in the sideways direction, expressed in MVC's legacy Unity-compatible units.
